item.research_question: What are the physical origins of the exceptional high-temperature strength and strength retention in refractory body-centered-cubic (BCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs)?
item.material_system: NbTaTiV (nominal Nb25Ta25Ti25V25 at.%) and CrMoNbV (nominal CrMoNbV at.%); search space includes the 10-component Al-Cr-Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-V-W-Zr family.
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt.% purity elements under argon atmosphere followed by drop-casting into cylindrical rods; NbTaTiV homogenized at 1473 K for 3 days then water-cooled; CrMoNbV tested in the as-cast state.
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial compression at strain rates of 1 × 10−3 s−1 (NbTaTiV) and 2 × 10−4 s−1 (CrMoNbV); temperatures up to 1173 K; in situ neutron diffraction and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) performed during deformation.
key_findings: Neutron diffraction peak broadening analysis yielded q values of -0.6 to -0.4 for NbTaTiV and -2 for CrMoNbV, consistent with edge dislocations and distinct from screw dislocations (+1.9 to +2.1).
Bright-field STEM stereographic analysis of NbTaTiV deformed at 293 K showed 75% (58 of 77) of dislocations were of edge character.
Bright-field STEM stereographic analysis of CrMoNbV deformed at 293 K showed 56% (23 of 41) of dislocations were of edge character.
At 1173 K, edge dislocations remained dominant with 82% (27 of 33) in NbTaTiV and 64% (81 of 127) in CrMoNbV.
The CrMoNbV alloy exhibited the highest reported strength at a homologous temperature of 1173 K.
A computationally guided search over 10^7 BCC HEA compositions identified over 10^6 possible ultra-strong high-temperature alloy compositions.
Theoretical predictions for NbTaTiV strength were lower than experimental values by ~300-500 MPa, attributed to 1.6 at.% O+N interstitial impurities.
item.mechanism: In complex HEAs, fluctuations in local solute arrangements create large local variations in potential energy, forcing edge dislocations to adopt a low-energy wavy structure; plastic flow requires thermal activation to overcome large energy barriers created by adjacent high-energy environments, enabling high strength retention at elevated temperatures.
item.limitations: The theory does not capture the strength plateau observed at 973–1273 K in many BCC HEAs; neutron pattern quality for CrMoNbV was lower than for NbTaTiV, especially at low plastic strains; the theory assumes a homogeneous average alloy which may not fully capture local complexities.
item.future_work: Propose fabrication and testing of specific alloys (Mo5W2.5CrZrHf, Mo2.5W2.5CrZrHf, Mo6WCrZrHf, Mo2.5TaWV2.5CrZrHf) with predicted strengths of ~2.5-3 GPa at 1300 K; combine design strategy with detailed thermodynamics and high ductility criteria to discover multi-objective alloys.
quotes: Here we show, using integrated in-situ neutron-diffraction (ND), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), and recent theory, that the high strength and strength retention of a NbTaTiV alloy and a high-strength/low-density CrMoNbV alloy are attributable to edge dislocations.
We use the insight and theory to perform a computationally-guided search over 107 BCC HEAs and identify over 106 possible ultra-strong high-T alloy compositions for future exploration.
